changes.text: 台谏请停修京通铁路；张之洞的议奏则排出修路之利的次序、列成条目，并把一条南北线路的北段、南段分给督抚。事情在传文里停在「得旨報可」四个字上。

The censors asked to halt the Beijing-Tongzhou railway. Zhang Zhidong's memorial ranked the benefits of building railways, set them out as numbered items, and assigned the northern and southern sections of a north-south line to governors-general and a governor. In the biography, the affair stops at four characters: approved by rescript.
要不要修京通铁路，朝中有了争执。《清史稿·张之洞传》记下这场争执只用了两句话：「會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦」。海军衙门主张修，台谏争陈铁路之害、请停办——至于害具体是哪几条，主张修的一方又答了什么，传文都没有抄录，只留下一个「請停辦」的收口。

The proposed Beijing-Tongzhou railway drew opposition at court. The Draft History of the Qing takes just two sentences over the dispute (here and throughout, quotations from the Chinese are our own translations): "When the Naval Office petitioned to build the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, the remonstrating officials pressed the harms of railways and asked that the project be halted." The Naval Office stood for building; the censors and remonstrating officials - the Qing court's remonstrance officials - pressed the harms and asked for a stop. Which harms, and what the other side answered, the biography never copies down. It closes on the bare "asked that the project be halted."
张之洞的议奏中明确排出了目标次序：「修路之利，以通土貨、厚民生為最大，徵兵、轉餉次之」。目标的轻重被明明白白摆上桌面——作者认为，这个排序是这篇议奏最容易被略过、也最见功夫的地方。

Zhang Zhidong's memorial set out an explicit ranking of goals: "In building a railway, the greatest benefit lies in moving local goods and enriching the people's livelihood; raising troops and forwarding supplies come second." The relative weight of the goals is laid plainly on the table. In the author's view, that ranking is the easiest thing to skim past in this memorial, and the place where the real craft sits.
在这之前，张之洞在广东办的是学堂、枪炮厂和矿务局。传文给这几件事安了一个前因：「之洞恥言和，則陰自圖強」，随后「設廣東水陸師學堂，創槍砲廠，開礦務局」。「恥言和」是《清史稿》修撰者写下的动机，并非本文推测。

Before this, Zhang had set up an academy, an arsenal, and a mining bureau in Guangdong. The biography gives those ventures a cause: "Ashamed of suing for peace, Zhidong quietly set about making himself strong," and then he founded the Guangdong Naval and Military Academy, created an arsenal, and opened a mining bureau. "Ashamed of suing for peace" is the motive the compilers of the Draft History assigned, not a conjecture of this article.
一种解释是，这个排序是有意为之：台谏争的是「鐵路之害」，若先论兵事，争执或许更烈（作者推测，传文未载）；把民生摆在前头，等于把辩论引到“土货通不通、民生厚不厚”这类可以逐条说的题目上。作者推断这只是顺序上的策略，传文并未写他这样排的理由。

One reading is that the ranking is deliberate. The censors were arguing "the harms of railways"; had he opened on military matters, the fight might have grown hotter (the author's conjecture; the biography does not say so). Placing livelihoods first steers the debate onto ground where points can be settled one by one - do local goods flow, do livelihoods thicken. The author infers this is tactics in the ordering; the biography records no reason of his own for the sequence.
议奏逐条列「利」，传文留下了编号：利一到利六，每条一两句。这组「利」是他自己列举的理由，不是独立核算过的数字；本文所据摘录列到「利六」，本文不替其余补写。

The memorial works through a numbered list of benefits, and the biography preserves the numbering: benefit one through benefit six, each a sentence or two. These are reasons he assembled himself, not figures from any independent accounting. The excerpt this article relies on runs to "benefit six," and this article will not write in anything beyond it.
前两条很朴素：「內處腹地，無慮引敵，利一；原野廣漠，墳廬易避，利二」。利一讲路在腹地、不至于引敌，利二讲原野开阔、坟墓与房屋容易避开。一种解释是，它们针对的是安全与迁坟拆屋的顾虑，但传文未记台谏所指何害。作者认为，值得记住的正是这半句：在一个「務宏大」的人笔下，最具体的落点是老百姓的坟和房子能不能绕开。

The first two are plain: "Situated in the interior, there is no fear of drawing in the enemy - benefit one; the open plains are broad, and graves and houses can easily be avoided - benefit two." Benefit one says the line lies in the interior and will not draw in an enemy; benefit two says the country is open, so graves and dwellings can easily be routed around. One reading is that they address worries about security and about moved graves and demolished homes, but the biography does not record which harms the censors meant. In the author's view, worth remembering is precisely that half-sentence: under the pen of a man the verdict calls "grand in scale," the most concrete landing point is whether ordinary people's graves and houses can be spared.
第三、四条转向生计与饷源：「廠盛站多，役夫賈客可舍舊圖新，利三；以一路控八九省之衢，人貨輻輳，足裕餉源，利四」。车站和工厂多起来，做工的人、跑买卖的人可以另谋出路；一条路控住八九省的要冲，人与货聚拢，饷源也就有了着落。作者认为，利三与「厚民生」相呼应；利四则落在饷源上。

Benefits three and four turn to livelihoods and revenue: "As works flourish and stations multiply, laborers and traders can leave the old for the new - benefit three; with one route commanding the crossroads of eight or nine provinces, people and goods converge, and the sources of military pay are made ample - benefit four." Hired hands and traveling merchants can find new lines of work; one line holds the crossroads of eight or nine provinces, people and goods crowd in, and revenue has somewhere to come from. In the author's view, benefit three echoes "enriching the people's livelihood"; benefit four lands on the sources of military pay.
第五条讲集兵，第六条讲煤铁开采：「近畿有事，淮、楚精兵崇朝可集，利五；太原旺煤鐵，運行便則開採必多，利六」。京畿一带有事，淮、楚精兵一早便可集结；太原煤铁旺盛，运输方便则开采必多。

Benefit five concerns gathering troops, benefit six coal and iron mining: "Should trouble arise near the capital, the picked troops of Huai and Chu can be gathered within a single morning - benefit five; Taiyuan is rich in coal and iron, and where transport is easy, mining will certainly increase - benefit six." If trouble arises in the region around the capital, the picked troops of Huai and Chu can assemble within a morning; Taiyuan is rich in coal and iron, and easier transport means more mining.
接着是接续图景。北路一段，「河北路成，則三晉之轍接於井陘，關隴之驂交於洛口」——山西的车辙接上井陉，关陇的车马交于洛口。南路一段，「自河以南，則東引淮、吳，南通湘、蜀，萬里聲息，刻期可通」。他没有停在一条线上，而是把议奏中的线路画成以河为界的南北两段、各自接上更大路网的样子。

Then comes the picture of connections. Of the northern stretch: "When the northern line is complete, the wheel-ruts of the Three Jin will meet at Jingxing, and the teams of Guan and Long will cross at Luokou" - Shanxi's cart-tracks connect at Jingxing, and the horse-teams of Guan and Long meet at Luokou. Of the southern stretch: "South of the river it will draw in Huai and Wu to the east and reach Xiang and Shu in the south; news from ten thousand li away can be carried on schedule." He does not stop at one line; he draws the line in his memorial as two stretches, north and south of the river, each hooking into a larger network.
再往下是分工：「北路責之直隸總督，南路責之湖廣總督，副以河南巡撫」。北路归直隶总督，南路归湖广总督，河南巡抚做副手。谁扛哪一段，写得清清楚楚，没有留下各段无人专责的余地。

Then the division of labor: "Let the northern section be the charge of the Governor-General of Zhili, and the southern section the charge of the Governor-General of Huguang, assisted by the Governor of Henan." Who carries which stretch is written out plainly, leaving no room for a section that no one is specifically responsible for.
结果是「得旨報可，遂有移楚之命」。朝廷准了这份奏请，随后有调他赴湖广之命。需要说清楚的是，「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工；传文没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁或争议后续，本文也不替他补。

The outcome: "The memorial received an approving rescript, and there followed the order transferring him to Huguang." The throne approved the request, and an order sending him to Huguang followed. Be clear: "approved by rescript" means the memorial was accepted, not that work began. The biography records no schedule, outlay, relocations, or aftermath of the dispute for the line he proposed, and this article will not supply them.
传文对他有一句评语：「蒞官所至，必有興作。務宏大，不問費多寡」。一种解释是，这句话与前面那份编号清单出自同一种风格——敢开大摊子，也肯把摊子一条条写出来；至于花费，评语说他不问多寡，传文并未举出具体用款数字。

The biography passes a verdict on him: "Wherever he took office, he had works begun. He aimed at the grand, and did not ask how much it cost." One reading: that verdict and the numbered list come from the same cast of mind - bold enough to open big undertakings, willing to write each out item by item. As for spending, the verdict says he did not ask the amount; the biography gives no figures.
作者的一种读法是，这份议奏包含三个部分：排目标次序（通土货、厚民生最大，征兵转饷次之），列逐条的「利」并编号，落实到官职（北路直隶总督、南路湖广总督、河南巡抚为副）。作者认为，这样写可能把争论从“有没有害”引向“这六条成不成立、这三位督抚之职扛不扛得动”。

One reading is that the memorial has three components: a ranking of goals (moving goods and enriching livelihoods greatest, raising troops and forwarding supplies next); a numbered, item-by-item list of benefits; and responsibility assigned to offices (north to the Governor-General of Zhili, south to the Governor-General of Huguang, the Governor of Henan as deputy). In the author's view, writing it this way may steer the argument away from "is it harmful" toward "do these six points hold, and can these three offices carry them."
首先，本文只依据《清史稿·张之洞传》一部传文，未用第二种记载对照。台谏所说的「鐵路之害」是哪几条、海军衙门的理由为何，传文一概未录，所以本文只能写到「爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦」为止。

First, this article relies on a single biography, that of Zhang Zhidong in the Draft History of the Qing, and has not checked it against a second record. Which harms the censors meant, and what reasons the Naval Office gave, the biography records not at all; so this article can go no further than "pressed the harms of railways and asked that the project be halted."
其次，那段议奏文字是史书所录的文字，未必是他逐字说过的话；本文所引文字均按史书所录转述。那组「利」是他自己列举的理由，不是独立核算过的数字，不能当作成本收益分析来读。

Second, the memorial text is documentary text as the historians recorded it, not necessarily words he spoke verbatim; all text quoted in this article is reported as the history records it. That set of "benefits" is a list of reasons he compiled himself, not independently audited figures, and cannot be read as cost-benefit analysis.
再次，传文没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁或争议后续，本文不替他补写；「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工，更不等于办成。本文也不把原文没有的公元年份换算出来，更不会说他事先知道结果——他写下那六条「利」的时候，看到的只是清单，不是成绩单。

Third, the biography records no schedule, outlay, relocations, or aftermath of the dispute for the proposed line, and this article does not fill them in. "Approved by rescript" is approval, not the start of work, still less a finished line. This article also converts no Common Era years the original does not have, and will not say he knew the outcome in advance: when he wrote those six benefits, what lay before him was a checklist, not a report card.
